angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 598,302 km at 156.40 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.3939 +/- 0.0153 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 156.40 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.86 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Lillo-Box et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-32 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...640A..48L/abstract): 598,302 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.83 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Lillo-Box et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-32 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...640A..48L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5271 +/- 39 K from Lillo-Box et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-32 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...640A..48L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lillo-Box et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-32 e in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...640A..48L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-32.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.488, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
